reviews.text: 简单但有意思，目前的内容量够玩2-3h吧，未来可期。

找一个按当前金钱数量加钱（猪猪），这把就开爽了，虽然描述上没写但是看起来是5%，升级只加一丢丢攻速，所以说数量多了比较舒服，最好卡在26个猪猪，然后你就可以看着你的钱1.05*1.05*1.05指数爆炸 利滚利滚利之后，就可以开始享受无限钱的乐趣了，全部升级拉满，防御塔全点橙色的，开爽就完事了。前期过渡塔不要拿太多，善用跳过功能，前期拿到的塔后面只会成为负担， 最后，单体防御塔全是垃圾，都别拿！包括紫色的点金手。白卡随便找2个aoe过渡，蓝卡最好是冰冻，紫卡最好是只拿黑洞，多的格子全上橙卡，爽就完了
0 meta, 0 progression between runs. Only 1 mode, endless.
单体塔太弱，过渡期容易暴毙，玩到3个小时后钱成负数没法玩了
This is the stupidly addictive misbegotten lovechild of Vampire Survivors and a Tower Defense game.
Nice take on the TD. Innovative and fun :)

The game visually isn't too much of a treat, the music selection will eventually loop on you and get old, and honestly the sprites are sorta too varied in quality, but man this game's concept of a on-rails vampire survivors-like with some really fun builds and run progression is too interesting and fun to not want to play more of it. Honestly I'd suggest to buy this at the current price, this seems like a good project to buy into before it gets big.

It gets better and better with each update, and it started off strong. This game is good; I recommend it. Also, the developers seem cool and want their game to be good. The additions keep coming, and now is a great time to jump in.

Fun for the price. Uncapped scaling of the turret upgrades is nice but ultimately let down by the UI/UX of the chests themselves. Having to click multiple buttons that are far apart in the ui makes opening chests in succession a huge pain. Keybindings, esc and b, arent much better.

Fun for a few hours if you´re really bored and itching that dopamine hit from numbers go higher. But honestly the endgame got nothing to offer aside from literally forcing you to click a bunch of times every 15-30seconds with an pretty annoying animation, to upgrade 1 weapon to the next lvl. which you could probably do for an infinite amount of hours. I assume the people that played it alot more hours, played it idle, that gets you nowhere, or just don´t realize how easily you can break the Game, just saying expotential growth - busts every game. Well anyway, expect 4-5 hours of fun till you break the game and go literally infinite while you´re down to watch a 5sec animation every 15 seconds. Might aswell still be a postive review btw. since i bought it for like 3,50, which is a fair amount for 3-4hours of fun, but decided to make it negative since it felt like to me, that development got entirely dropped or given up upon, concering balancing after you make it to "Endgame"

fun for a little while. for the price it´s okay. - edit/ even for the low price, it is not OK. i regret playing this for more than 8 hours. i wanted to see whether it would go anywhere. other than repetitive strain injury, you get nothing out of this game. gets a bit boring soon When about an hour and a half in, it starts to look like work (when upgrading towers, need to roll,buy click click click hundreds of times.) Here you can see it comming, next round of upgrading will require thousands of click click sequences) --- edit- I regret playing this. You will reach a few points where you need to spend actual hours of clicking for tower upgrades.

I actively played for 20 minutes; then stepped a way for a moment and forgot to come back; the game had run by itself for just under 2 hours before being overrun. I don't see much effort having been put into making the gameplay challenging. After exiting that game I had unlocked quite a few buffs and boons; what challenge are those supposed to help me overcome, running it unattended for 6 hours? Not worthy of the v1.0 release; still feels WAY early access.
Fun at first but without any automation gameplay becomes just clicking level ups for turrets.

Eventually, you spend half of your time waiting for the "All In" animation delay saying "ARE YOU READY?" "HERE WE GO", "SUCCESS". If you get rid of the super long animations on All In, this game would be so much more fun. It's wayyy too slow.

A very simple tower defence game which is reminiscent of old browser games. The overall gameplay loop and controls are too minimalistic for my tastes thou. You only try to roll multiples of 3 for each wagon and that is it. A bit of a missed chance in my opinion with boring upgrades, uninteresting progression between runs. Add some automation or more ways to control the buying/upgrading. Add different track and map layouts.

This is a tower defense/idle game where you buy upgrades for a train as it defends a central tower. While there is a train not much is done with the concept. You buy "carriages" instead of towers but they function the same as the track is a never changing circle and you don't decide where to place them, where the track goes or anything like that. You choose what type of carriages to buy whether thats gold producing ones, or a sniper, or AOE cannon, and when you have enough low level ones they combine into a higher level one. All fine in theory. But in the mid game, usually around 30 minutes or so into a run you have an insane amount of gold vs. what it costs to buy a carriage. You are supposed to utilize the "all-in" mechanic but that is SO inefficient that its usually not an actual option till much later. So without that mechanic you have to manually buy 100s, maybe 1000s, of individual carriages one at a time. This is beyond tedious. The "all-in" mechanic that is supposed to fix this feels like an after thought so just does not function well and you will literally just lose if you try and use it too early. Even if you could get past that glaring problem, the pacing is also crap. My first run took maybe 10 minutes. My second around 30 minutes. But then on the next run a fairy spawned giving me an absurd amount of resources and the run lasted for 5 hours, 90% of which was just letting the game idle. After that run I unlocked almost everything in the game, and the meta currency of "tickets" became worthless to me. Worst of all I let the game run at x2 speed (5 hours in game time, so maybe 2 1/2 real time?) but that unlocked the x3 speed, That x3 speed would have been nice to have for that absurd idle run. It just seemed like the game was not prepared for me to have that many resources that quickly, which ruined much of my desire to grind. And of course grinding is all there is. Lastly, while the game is mostly about the gameplay, the art direction is pretty garbage too. The train carriages look super basic and utilitarian, the mobs are simple, and since you basically have to play at least at the x2 speed, everything blurs together. It looks like primary color soup. The one solitary compliment I can pay this game is that the music is actually quite good, with a few nice tracks. Bottomline is that the basic idea of the game is fine, but with poor balance and glaring gameplay issues, there is no reason to play it.

I downloaded this as a joke thinking this is just a silly little train game. That was 6 hours ago. I have missed a meal. My legs are asleep. I think I might be dehydrated. This game is the digital equivalent of gas station energy drinks. It is cheap, it kills your brain cells, and it is absolutely delicious.

Its like a more exciting version of tism Nascar watching the train go round and round again and blastin up goons. While the base game play loop is just buy better weapons to survive each wave of goobers it is still a good ole time. I do love the massive variety on the weapons, however some very clearly far outstrip others in performance which is a vibe kill. It is nice that you can just let the game AFK for hours on end after you get to a certain level of strength where you neednt worry about your run suddenly ending, but at that point you have likely already achieved your initial goal of the run. All Aboard is definitely a fun take on the survivors genre and for the price this is a fantastic game that will keep you semi occupied for many hours to come. HIghly recommend people give this game a try.

this game is seriously better than I was expecting, the gameplay is generally engaging enough, and just as you start to slow down you unlock All-In, which opens up the game so much. This game has the same vibe energy as games like Risk Of Rain 2, truly letting you push it to the limits with no level cap, or cap on relics. A noticeable mention to the performance of said game, running flawlessly on my very low end PC, and the file size is a work of art, as I'm always one to appreciate such a large game packed into about 100MB! Highly recommend for a great time
